theme: 3 terms on passing blocks of code around

terms.definition: A block of code you can store in a variable or pass to a function and run later.
terms.example: I passed a closure to the sort method so it knows how to compare two names.

terms.definition: A closure written after the function's parentheses instead of inside them, which makes the call easier to read.
terms.example: I used a trailing closure on map, so the code reads cleanly with no extra parentheses.

terms.definition: A list in square brackets at the start of a closure that says which outside values the closure keeps, and how it keeps them.
terms.example: I added a capture list with weak self so the closure does not keep the view controller alive.

quizzes.question: Which one is written in square brackets at the start of a closure to control how it keeps outside values?
Which one is a block of code you can store in a variable and run later?

video.title: Closure, Trailing Closure & Capture List | iOS Daily English Day 7
video.description:
Learn to talk about closures in Swift: Closure, Trailing Closure and Capture List, with a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Closure - A block of code you can store in a variable or pass to a function and run later.
Trailing Closure - A closure written after the function's parentheses instead of inside them, which makes the call easier to read.
Capture List - A list in square brackets at the start of a closure that says which outside values the closure keeps, and how it keeps them.

Quiz at the end - comment your answers, then watch again to check.
